column6: Separating variables in Laplace's equation in polar coordinates gives a Cauchy-Euler equation, not Bessel's; changed to the Helmholtz (drumhead) equation with x = λr

Note only, not edited: "can generally be made exact by an integrating factor" is keyed false, but an integrating factor exists locally under mild conditions; the item conflates existence with findability
P(x) > 0 implies y_h always decays is false (P = 1/x² has a finite integral); changed the hypothesis to P(x) ≥ k > 0; also softened the matching parenthetical in q:3 explanation
Answer key was (2/L) option; a₁ = (1/L)∫f cos(πx/L) dx under either a₀ convention; answer set to 1 and explanation corrected
Stem "typically converges to f(x) at most point" is true for piecewise smooth f, yet keyed false; restored to "always converges ... at every point", which matches the key and explanation
Bullet 3 ("partial fractions can be skipped if you can guess") was not a misconception: its correction opened "You can"; deleted, 2 bullets remain
Old explainer contains banned word "genuinely" (line 80); left, out of scope
Typo eˡ for eᵗ in the worked example
Claimed a Neumann condition determines the solution uniquely; it does so only up to an added constant
Said defective (Jordan) nodes "spiral mildly"; they bend toward the single eigenvector without spiraling
Simple harmonic oscillator with non-constant forcing listed as a variable-coefficient ODE (forcing is not a coefficient); replaced with Airy's equation
w'' = 0, so w is constant is wrong (w'' = 0 gives linear w); the reduced equation is v'' = 0, i.e. w' = 0
Tacoma Narrows presented as resonance; the accepted cause is aeroelastic flutter, now stated
